title: nautilus project manifest
description: A manifest-defined nautilus controller: tasks, tags by role, the server, and a configured field driver. Pure data — anything needing computation is generated upstream and committed. Secrets are NEVER in this file: NAUTILUS_TOKEN and NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD come from the environment.

name.description: The controller's name. Defaults to "nautilus"; also the default Sparkplug edge-node id and the default output name for `naut build`.

plant.description: The plant model file (plant.yaml): areas, equipment (a declared tag or a devices: row each, with an asset type) and the flows between them, with asset types in asset-types/*.asset.yaml beside it. Mimics and scenes name a piece of equipment with `plant:`; `naut hmi build` writes an asset page for each. Absent, nothing changes. See docs/design/plant-model.md.

dialect.description: Opt into a vendor-semantics block library: `logix` adds blocks with Allen-Bradley semantics (TONR, …) written in nautilus, so the runtime runs them and the Logix writer/importer map them to the native instructions. Default `nautilus` adds nothing; `siemens` and `codesys` are reserved.

server.description: The tag API an HMI reads.

tasks.description: One program per scan. The FIRST task is the main task: it owns field I/O and is the default online-edit target.

tag-files.description: Files holding additional tags, each a bare YAML list of the same entries as `tags`. This is where a GENERATED tag set lives, so it stays a separate reviewable artifact instead of a 500-line smear through the file you edit — and how one project ships to several sites, by choosing which tag files a site's manifest composes. Read in order, then `tags` last. A tag declared twice in any two sources is an error: fix the generator, or narrow its scope.

tags.description: Tags declared by role. Hand-authored tags belong here; bulk or generated sets belong in a file listed under `tag-files`.

tag-meta.description: HMI documentation layered onto tags declared elsewhere, keyed by tag name or by a dotted field path (`P101.Speed`). Use it when a generator cannot supply documentation — `naut eip import` cannot, because Logix keeps tag descriptions in the offline project file. A generator that HAS descriptions should emit them into its tag file instead. This reaches only unit and desc: it can never change what the controller does.

driver.description: The field driver. Defaults to "memory", the loopback used for bring-up. For more than one bus on the same scan, use drivers: instead — setting both is an error.

drivers.description: Several field drivers on one scan — e.g. an EtherNet/IP poll plus a Sparkplug feed. Each entry is the same shape as driver:, plus an optional name to tell status rows apart. A tag may be owned by exactly one driver; a duplicate is a load-time error naming both. One entry behaves exactly like driver:. Do not set driver: as well.

devices.description: Field devices declared by profile (the device library). Each row derives, at load, one struct tag typed by its profile (its members read back the device), a command tag <name>_<point> per writable point, and its driver bindings. The profile must be vendored in profiles/ (naut devices add <profile>). Modbus devices join the project's Modbus driver; one is added if there is none.

name.description: What a READ or WRITE block's ID names. Unique (case-insensitively).

type.description: cip: a Logix controller over EtherNet/IP (the services a Logix MSG of type CIP Data Table Read/Write sends).

slot.description: Route to the processor in this backplane slot behind host: a ControlLogix CPU reached through an Ethernet module. Leave it out for a controller with its own Ethernet port (a CompactLogix); a written MSG then ends at host.

timeout.description: How long one request may take before it fails with STATUS -3 (default 5s).

queue.description: How many requests may wait before one fails with STATUS -5 (default 64).

channels.description: Communication channels for the programs' READ and WRITE blocks (IEC 61131-5): one peer each. A driver moves the same tags every scan; a channel moves one variable when a program asks. naut check errors on a READ or WRITE whose ID names no channel here.

opcua.description: Serve the tag store as an OPC UA address space. Any OPC UA client browses, reads and subscribes to the tags; a trusted client also writes the tags writable opens. The section's presence turns the server on.

sparkplug.description: Republish the tag store as a Sparkplug B edge node.

parameters.description: How operator-tuned setpoint values get back to Git (#718). Absent, drift is only reported (GET /api/parameters).

writeBack.description: off: report only. patch: GET /api/parameters/patch returns the plant-ahead values as a patch. commit: a controller running from a git checkout commits them itself (one commit per editor, after 30 s of quiet or 50 pending), editing only each tag's init:.

retain.description: Persist operator state (setpoints, online edits) across restarts: a ConfigMap in a cluster, a JSON file anywhere else. An empty mapping takes both defaults.

file.description: JSON file path outside a cluster (default retain.json).

audit.description: The runtime audit journal `naut run` always keeps: every action that changes something (tag writes, forces, alarm acks, online edits), accepted or refused, as one fsynced, hash-chained line. `naut audit verify` checks it. This section only moves it or changes how long it is kept.

path.description: The journal's directory (default audit, in the working directory).

keep-days.description: Days of journal files kept (default 365). A negative number keeps every file.

sink.description: Keep a copy of the journal in Postgres (the audit_entries table) for queries and export. It tails the files and catches up after any outage; the files stay the source of truth.

dsn-env.description: The environment variable holding the copy's connection string (default NAUTILUS_AUDIT_DB_URL, then DATABASE_URL). Never the connection string itself.

anchor-every.description: How often the copy anchors the journal's head in Postgres when it has moved (default 5m, at least 1s), a duration such as 5m. It also anchors at start, after every prune and at a clean stop; naut audit verify --anchor postgres checks the journal against the anchors.

auth.description: Who may do what (#708): roles, areas, users and service tokens, reviewed in git. Credentials never go here. Absent, writes keep today's rule (the auth token when one is set, else a same-origin request).

anonymous.description: What a request with no credential may do: none (the default: sign-in required) or viewer (a wallboard).

token-role.description: NAUTILUS_TOKEN's role (default administrator): a built-in role (viewer, operator, supervisor, engineer, administrator) or one under roles.

areas.description: Named sets of tags that scope a grant's write, ack, shelve, note, substitute and force.

tags.description: Tag patterns (RCV_*), matched ignoring case against a tag's name.

roles.description: Custom roles: one to inherit, plus permissions to allow or deny.

inherits.description: The role this one starts from: viewer, operator, supervisor, engineer, administrator, or another custom role.

users.description: Each user's grants: a role, or {role, areas}. No secrets here.

oidc.description: Browser sign-in at an OpenID Connect provider (Entra ID, Google, Keycloak, Okta). A person acts as oidc:<name> (the username claim), pinned to their account at the provider on first sign-in (naut users unpin undoes it). The client secret comes from NAUTILUS_OIDC_SECRET, never the manifest. Not on a redundant pair yet.

issuer.description: The provider's issuer URL: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0, https://accounts.google.com, https://<keycloak>/realms/<realm>.

client-id.description: The client (application) id the provider registered for this controller.

name.description: The sign-in button's label (Sign in with <name>). Default from the issuer: Microsoft, Google, else its host.

username-claim.description: The ID token claim that names a person (the display and journal name). Default preferred_username.

groups-claim.description: The ID token claim that lists a person's group ids. Default groups.

groups.description: Grants by group id, as the groups claim carries it (an Entra object id, a Keycloak group path), never a display name: a role, or grants as a user's ({role, areas}).

users.description: Grants by name (the username claim's value, matched ignoring case), for a provider that sends no groups: a role, or grants as a user's ({role, areas}).

redirect-url.description: The callback URL registered at the provider: https://<this controller's host>/auth/oidc/callback. Without it the controller builds it from a trusted Host (NAUTILUS_ALLOWED_HOSTS); naut run prints it at the start.

state-dir.description: Where the controller keeps its users file (users.json: password hashes and personal access tokens, managed with naut users). Default: systemd's $STATE_DIRECTORY. Never inside the project, so no hash reaches git.

session.description: How long a browser sign-in lasts, from the sign-in (not renewed by use): 1m to 168h. Default 12h. Sessions live in the leader's memory: a restart or a failover signs browser users out.

elevation.description: How long a browser sign-in's password counts for the elevated permissions (force, edit, activate, deploy, config, users, override), from the sign-in or the last re-authentication (POST /api/elevate), not renewed by use: 1m to 12h. Default 15m. A token always counts as elevated.

service-tokens.description: Named tokens for scripts and services: each a role, or grants as a user's ({role, areas}). A token's secret comes from NAUTILUS_TOKEN_<NAME>, never the manifest.

sparkplug.description: What a Sparkplug command (NCMD/DCMD) may do: a role, or grants as a service token's ({role, areas}). A command write needs sparkplug.writable AND write on the tag's area. Without this key, under auth: every command write is refused (Node Control/Rebirth still works). A command is journalled as sparkplug:<primary-host, else the broker's host>: a label, not a proof, since anyone who can publish to the broker can send one.

opcua-certificates.description: OPC UA client certificates mapped to roles: each names exactly one of a thumbprint (the 40-digit SHA-1 `naut opcua certs` prints) or a subject (as it prints it), and grants as a service token's. Such a session writes as opcua-cert:<name>, within those grants. Under auth: a trusted certificate not named here writes nothing: its client signs in with a user name to write.

redundancy.description: Lease-based leader election: replicas elect one scanning leader, the rest stand by. Standalone (always leader) outside a cluster. An empty mapping takes the default lease name.

lease.description: coordination.k8s.io Lease name (default: the project name).

checkout.description: The I/O checkout and commissioning sign-off (#719): the sheet of points, and who may seal a run.

file.description: The sheet, relative to the project. Default checkout.yaml (naut checkout init writes one).

real-io.description: Names of drivers and devices that reach real field I/O although the controller cannot tell from the endpoint (a local gateway on a loopback address, a driver whose hosts are in a manifest file). Without them the controller refuses to sign off a run against loopback, virtual or unreadable endpoints.

signoff.description: Who may seal a run: two-person (the default) needs a signer who recorded none of its results; single lets the person who recorded them sign, naut check warns and the sealed record says single-person.

pwa.description: Names and themes the installed HMI (progressive web app). Every field is optional: an HMI naut builds is installable without this section. Installing and the offline shell need HTTPS (or localhost): a controller on plain LAN HTTP cannot be installed from a phone.

name.description: The installed app's name. Default: the project's name.

short-name.description: The label under the icon (about 12 characters). Default: name.

theme-color.description: Browser chrome and splash color, "#rrggbb". Default: the kit's dark background.

icon.description: A square PNG of 512 pixels or more, in the project. Default: a drawn icon in the theme color.

alarm-files.description: Files holding additional alarm definitions and rules, each a bare YAML list. Mirrors `tag-files:` exactly, and for the same reason: a GENERATED alarm set stays a separate reviewable artifact. Read in order, then `alarms:` last. An id declared twice in any two sources is an error naming both.

check.description: Settings for the diagram structure warnings `naut check` and the editor report on ladder, FBD and SFC (LD001…, FBD001…, SFC001…): thresholds, and rules switched off for the whole project. One POU opts out with an `(* @allow ID: reason *)` pragma in its header instead. See the Structure warnings reference.

disable.description: Rule IDs not reported in this project.

max-series.description: LD003: the most condition elements in series on one rung (a branch counts as its longest leg).

max-branch-depth.description: LD002: how deep ladder branches may nest (1: a branch, but no branch inside a leg).

max-nesting.description: FBD001: how deep FBD calls may nest in one statement (an FB call counts as a level).

target.description: A controller this project is DEPLOYED to instead of being run by the nautilus runtime. With a target set, `naut check` also runs that target's rules. One kind at a time. Experimental: docs/design/logix-authoring.md, docs/design/siemens-ide.md.

logix.description: An Allen-Bradley Logix controller, written as an L5X project by `naut logix deploy` and reached through a logixd agent on the licensed Studio 5000 machine.

controller.description: Logix controller (project) name. Default: the task program's POU name.

comm-path.description: FactoryTalk Linx path logixd uses to reach the controller, e.g. AB_ETH-1\10.0.0.5\Backplane\0. Required to deploy.

host.description: The controller's EtherNet/IP address, for live values (`naut logix serve`).

agent.description: logixd URL. NAUTILUS_LOGIXD_URL overrides it; the token is never in the manifest (NAUTILUS_LOGIXD_TOKEN).

program.description: Logix program name (default: the POU name).

task.description: Task the program is scheduled in (default MainTask).

continuous.description: Schedule the program in a CONTINUOUS Logix task, as the controller it was imported from did; the task's scan: is then only nautilus's own rate. Default false: a PERIODIC task at scan:.

all-tags.description: Write every manifest tag as a controller tag, whether or not a program names it, as `naut logix import` sets for a project whose tag file is the controller's tag set: a tag only an external client reads or writes is still the controller's. Default false: a tag no program names is not written. A tag with neither type: nor init: has no type to write either way, and an unnamed one whose type the Logix subset lacks (a STRING) is left out.

controller-scoped.description: Program variables written as controller tags rather than program tags. `naut logix import` lists a timer or counter the export had at controller scope (a block instance is program-scoped in nautilus), so the write-back keeps its tag path (AcceptTmr.ACC, not Program:MainProgram.AcceptTmr.ACC) and its description.

name.description: A VAR of the task program.

messages.description: What a Logix MSG holds that a READ or WRITE block and its channel do not, per instance, so the write-back gives each MESSAGE tag back as `naut logix import` found it. Only values that differ from the writer's defaults are listed.

name.description: A READ or WRITE instance of the task program.

connection-path.description: MessageParameters ConnectionPath, verbatim, when the export spells it other than the channel's "2, host[, 1, slot]".

hardware.description: An L5X, relative to the project, whose <Modules> section is the controller's I/O configuration: the chassis, its modules, and the adapters and modules beyond it that alias: tags name. The writer carries it into every project it writes, unchanged, in place of the controller's generated Local module, and refuses an alias of a rack point whose module it lacks (logix/io-module). `naut logix import --project` writes one, hardware.L5X, from an export with I/O modules; a Logix Designer export of the whole project works as it is. Its Local module must be the target's processor at the target's revision.

side.description: Side code nautilus adds beside the program, in a Logix program of its own (Nautilus): testing, verification and metrics logic that never touches the user's routine.

heartbeat.description: Name of a controller DINT the side program increments once per task scan; `naut test --target logix` waits on it for an exact `scans: n`.

substitutes.description: Inputs a person may run the program on a chosen value for while the real sensor is bad or wrong (a stuck level switch reads Good and wrong), for a bounded time, flagged everywhere (quality `substituted`, the <tag>__Substituted tag) and audited. Not alarm shelving, and not a force.

rules.description: Tried in order; the first rule that matches an input decides it.

substitute-defaults.description: What a rule gets for a key it leaves out.

role.description: The role allowed to start one (default supervisor). Shown by the API; enforced when roles land (#708).

ack-on-start.description: The program's start interlock waits (__SubstitutesUnacked) until the substitute is acknowledged. Default false.

operator-value.description: A person may choose the value at start (checked against the tag's type). Default false: the engineer chose the safe value.

match.description: An input tag name or glob (case-insensitive). A name with a dot (IOL_P3.Level) substitutes one member of each matching struct tag.

substitute.description: The value the program runs on. Checked against the tag's type as a write is.

role.description: The role allowed to start one.

ack-on-start.description: Wait for an acknowledgement of this substitute before the program's start interlock opens.

operator-value.description: A person may choose the value at start.

name.description: The device's tag name: a struct tag of the profile's type. Command tags are <name>_<point>; the driver's companions are <name>__Online and <name>__Outages.

profile.description: A profile id vendored in profiles/<id>.yaml (naut devices add <id>; naut devices profiles lists the built-in ones).

endpoint.description: Where the device answers: a Modbus host[:port] (the port defaults to the profile's, then 502), or an OPC UA host[:port] or opc.tcp://host[:port] (the port defaults to the profile's, then 4840).

unit-id.description: The Modbus unit id; defaults to the profile's. An OPC UA device has none.

points.description: Globs over point names: the points this device polls and has as members of its struct (default: all). Devices of one type select the same points.

desc.description: One line for the device's tags.

driver.description: An OPC UA device's connection: the name of an opcua-client section of drivers: with no endpoint or manifest (a template), whose security, security-mode, pki-dir, username, read-mode and scan-rate the device's own driver takes. Several devices may share one. Without it the device connects with security None, anonymous, and naut check says so. Not on a Modbus device.

validate.description: How a live I/O configuration change checks this device: live probes it on a connection of its own, static checks the configuration only. Overrides the driver's validate:. Default: static when the profile documents modbus max-connections of 2 or fewer, else live. live on a profile documenting max-connections 1 is an error.

name.description: The port's device tag, unique among the project's devices and ports.

iodd.description: The sensor's IODD: a file name in the project's iodd/ folder.

ports.description: An IO-Link master's ports by number: the sensor on each. Only a profile that declares IO-Link ports takes them.

duration.description: A Go duration: "250ms", "2s", "1h30m". A bare number is not one — the unit is required.

addr.description: Listen address for the tag API (default "localhost:8080"). NAUTILUS_ADDR overrides at start.

online-edits.description: Allow a running controller's program to be replaced without a restart.

interval.description: How often the server pushes tag updates to connected clients.

historian.description: Base URL of a `naut historian` daemon; GET /api/history* proxies there. NAUTILUS_HISTORIAN_URL overrides.

hmi.description: A built HMI's directory, relative to the project (e.g. the SvelteKit `adapter-static` output, "./hmi/build") — must resolve inside the project, like every other manifest-referenced path. When set, the controller serves it at "/" (falling back to its index.html for a client-side route), and the built-in dashboard moves to "/_nautilus/". The HMI must call the tag API same-origin (a relative "/api/..." base URL).

tls.description: The certificate the tag API serves (HTTPS): self-signed (the controller makes one in its state directory; browsers warn until accepted; not on a redundant pair), or PEM files on the box at absolute paths outside the project (a private key never belongs in git), re-read when they change. NAUTILUS_TLS_CERT and NAUTILUS_TLS_KEY override either.

oneOf.description: A certificate the controller makes on its first start, in its state directory, and naut run renews from 30 days before its expiry (at its start, and daily while it runs). naut run prints its SHA-256 fingerprint.

cert.description: The certificate (chain) file, PEM, absolute path.

key.description: The private key file, PEM, absolute path; not readable by every user on the box.

trusted-proxies.description: Addresses or prefixes ("127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.0/24") of a TLS-terminating proxy in front of the controller (tailscale serve, nginx): only from these is X-Forwarded-Proto: https believed (Secure cookies, password sign-in) and X-Forwarded-For used as the client's address in the audit journal. Empty: none.

task.description: One program on its own scan.

name.description: Identifies the task in status and acceptance tests. Defaults to the program's filename. "main" is reserved for the first task.

program.description: The program file in this project — normally .st, .fbd, .ld, or .sfc. The loader requires a PROGRAM declaration inside it, not a particular extension, so none is enforced here.

dt-tag.description: Tag to publish this task's measured scan delta into, for logic that integrates over real elapsed time.

late-threshold.description: How late a scan may start before the runtime diagnostics count it as late (the lateness block on /api/state). Default: a tenth of scan. Set on the first task, it is also the default for every task without its own.

cpu.description: Pin this task's scan thread to one CPU (Linux sched_setaffinity). The core is only quiet if the kernel was told to keep everything else off it (isolcpus=, nohz_full=, irqaffinity=) — see docs/design/realtime.md.

priority.description: Run this task's thread under SCHED_FIFO at this priority (Linux). Needs CAP_SYS_NICE (setcap cap_sys_nice+ep on the binary) or an rtprio rlimit; a refused request is logged and shown in the task's stats, and the task runs at normal priority.

share-cpu.description: Pin to cpu: even where another program already runs a real-time thread above this task's priority (a vendor runtime or I/O shim, most likely), which is otherwise refused at start, with the task running unpinned at normal priority. Default false.

priority-guard.description: Bounds the task while it runs at priority: past either bound its thread goes back to normal scheduling until a restart, logged and shown in its scan.sched, so a runaway task cannot starve its core. Leave it out for the defaults.

overruns.description: Scans in a row that each take longer than the period. Default 50.

scan-multiple.description: One scan in progress for longer than this many periods. Default 20.

rt-limit.description: How long a real-time thread may run without blocking before the kernel's RLIMIT_RTTIME demotes every task with priority:, from 10ms to 200ms: it only tightens the 200ms default, never loosens it. One limit per process: the strictest of every task's rt-limit and NAUTILUS_RT_LIMIT_MS is the one in force. Only on a task with priority:.

tag.description: One tag, declared by the role it plays in the scan data path.

name.description: The tag name. ST binds it with VAR_EXTERNAL; the driver and HMI address it by this name.

role.description: input: driver → tag each scan, deliberately unseeded so a missing value faults loudly. output: tag → driver each scan; with a type it starts at that type's zero, else add init when the logic reads it back. setpoint: seeded operator/config value. state: seeded logic-owned value (latches, integrators).

type.description: The tag's data type: an IEC elementary type (BOOL, SINT, INT, DINT, LINT, USINT, UINT, UDINT, ULINT, BYTE, WORD, DWORD, LWORD, REAL, LREAL, TIME, STRING), a TYPE this project's ST declares (a UDT), or an ARRAY[lo..hi] OF either. Every program sees the tag with this type without declaring it; a VAR_EXTERNAL naming it must agree. init must agree with it too. A typed setpoint or state needs no init: zero-of-type is its seed. A typed input stays unseeded, so a driver that has not delivered still faults loudly.

init.description: Initial value. A scalar for an untyped (or scalar-typed) tag; a TIME as T#2s, 2s or milliseconds; a list for an ARRAY (from its lower bound). Without a type:, the init also types the tag every program sees: TRUE/FALSE BOOL, a number REAL, T#… TIME, other text STRING. For a struct-typed tag (`type:`), init may instead be a mapping of member name to value — nested for a member that is itself a struct — to seed only the members that need a non-zero starting value; every member the mapping omits still takes the zero of its own field type. A struct-typed tag given a scalar init is an error. Required for setpoint and state unless `type` supplies one. On an output, needed only when the logic reads it before writing it (a seal-in latch).

unit.description: Engineering unit shown by an HMI ("°C", "%", "L/s").

desc.description: Human description shown in tag tables.

alias.description: Vendor-side binding of this tag: on a Logix target the alias tag's AliasFor ("Local:1:I.Data.3"), which is how a Logix program names a rack point. The nautilus runtime ignores it. The one place a hardware address lives in a project.

retain.description: Keep this tag's value across a restart in the retain store, as CODESYS VAR RETAIN does: for state the logic owns, such as run hours or a start count. Setpoints are always kept. Needs a retain: section. Not for an input or an output.

min.description: Lowest value an external write (HMI, API, Sparkplug, OPC UA) may set on this setpoint; a lower one is refused. The program's own writes are never refused. Setpoints only; init must not be below it.

max.description: Highest value an external write (HMI, API, Sparkplug, OPC UA) may set on this setpoint; a higher one is refused. The program's own writes are never refused. Setpoints only; init must not be above it.

meta.description: Documentation for one tag or one field of a tag.

unit.description: Engineering unit shown by an HMI ("°C", "%", "L/s").

desc.description: Human description shown in tag tables.

name.description: Names this driver in status rows and error messages when several share a drivers: list (default: its type, deduped "eip-2"). Inert on a lone driver: section.

type.description: memory: loopback for bring-up, so logic and HMI run before hardware exists. eip: polls an Allen-Bradley Logix controller. sparkplug-host: consumes a Sparkplug B group as a host application, presenting every edge node's metrics as tags. modbus: polls a set of Modbus TCP sources with coalesced block reads. opcua-client: the OPC UA client — polls one OPC UA server (an Ignition gateway's, a PLC's embedded one, a Kepware) per scan class from a manifest `naut opcua import` writes; not the top-level opcua: section, which serves this project's tags. snmp / redfish / prometheus: IT hardware as tags — switches, PDUs and UPSes over SNMP, server BMCs over Redfish, hosts over node_exporter — generated manifests, credentials from the environment. plcnext: the runtime running ON a Phoenix Contact PLCnext controller, driving its local Axioline I/O through the firmware's data-access socket (BusConductor process image). optommp: an Opto 22 groov EPIC or groov RIO chassis over OptoMMP (TCP 2001) — every channel's state or value with per-channel quality, outputs, optional counters, latches, quality codes and scratchpad — from the LAN or from nautilus running on the EPIC itself (127.0.0.1); manifest from `naut optommp import`. profinet-device: nautilus as a PROFINET IO device to a PLC (RT, one AR) on a raw-Ethernet interface; the PLC's outputs are input tags and its inputs output tags, laid out by the profinet_device.yaml, whose GSDML `naut profinet gsdml` writes; needs CAP_NET_RAW. replay: a recorded history played back as the same IT-hardware tags at a clock the project steers (Replay_Speed, Replay_Pause, Replay_SeekS) — the baseline of a plant simulation. Custom buses are the Go tier.

host.description: eip: controller IP or hostname, optionally "host:port" to reach it off the standard EtherNet/IP port 44818 (e.g. `naut logix emulate` running on 127.0.0.1:44818, or a nonstandard port on a real controller). A bare host keeps the default port.

manifest.description: eip: the imported tag manifest, generated by `naut eip import --format yaml`. sparkplug-host: the imported Sparkplug manifest, generated by `naut sparkplug import`. modbus: the imported modbus manifest (sources and register bindings), generated by `naut modbus import` (or by `naut optommp import --modbus` from a groov EPIC chassis). optommp: the optommp_manifest.yaml generated by `naut optommp import`. opcua-client: the opcua_manifest.yaml (node bindings) generated by `naut opcua import`. plcnext: the plcnext_manifest.yaml binding tags to byte and bit offsets of the controller's process image. profinet-device: the profinet_device.yaml (interface, station, identity, slots and tag offsets). Any path the project can read; no extension is enforced.

scan-rate.description: eip / modbus / opcua-client / optommp / plcnext: default poll period for bound tags.

scan-classes.description: eip / modbus / opcua-client: named poll groups and their periods.

tag-classes.description: eip / modbus / opcua-client: glob patterns assigning tags to a scan class. Overrides the generated manifest, so imports stay regenerable and policy stays here.

validate.description: modbus / opcua-client: how a live I/O configuration change checks this driver's devices: live probes each changed device on a connection of its own before the apply, static checks the configuration only. A devices: row's own validate: overrides it. Default: the device profile's (static when it documents modbus max-connections of 2 or fewer), else live.

broker.description: sparkplug-host: broker URL, e.g. tcp://host:1883 or ssl://host:8883. The MQTT password is NEVER here — set NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD.

group-id.description: sparkplug-host: the Sparkplug group_id to consume.

group-ids.description: sparkplug-host: consume several groups. Overrides group-id.

host-id.description: sparkplug-host: this host application's id — it owns the STATE topic spBv1.0/STATE/<host-id>, which is what edge nodes gate their births on.

username.description: sparkplug-host: MQTT username (password from NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD). opcua-client: UserName token (password from NAUTILUS_OPCUA_PASSWORD). The password is NEVER here.

primary.description: sparkplug-host: publish the STATE certificate and send commands (default true). false makes this a passive consumer that only reads.

state-form.description: sparkplug-host: which STATE certificate to publish — the Sparkplug 3.0 retained JSON (default), the legacy 2.x retained ONLINE/OFFLINE text, or both for a mixed fleet.

reorder-timeout.description: sparkplug-host: how long an unfilled sequence gap waits before the host asks that node to rebirth (default 5s).

stale-after.description: sparkplug-host: mark a node stale after this much silence. Omit to disable.

on-unknown.description: sparkplug-host: what to do with a metric on the wire the manifest does not bind — log it once with the YAML line to add (default), count it only, or report the driver degraded. Never silently dropped; the remedy is to re-run the import.

rebirth-on-start.description: sparkplug-host: ask every manifest node to rebirth on connect (default true). Births are not retained, so a host starting mid-stream sees nothing until it asks.

rebirth-requests.description: sparkplug-host: send NCMD Rebirth requests at all (default true) — on connect, on reconnect, on data before a birth, after a sequence gap. false sends none; with primary: false the host then publishes nothing (a read-only broker account) and waits for births another host asks for.

endpoint.description: opcua-client: the server URL to poll, e.g. opc.tcp://10.0.0.5:4840. This URL is dialled even when the server advertises another.

security.description: opcua-client: security policy — None, Basic128Rsa15, Basic256, Basic256Sha256, Aes128_Sha256_RsaOaep, Aes256_Sha256_RsaPss. Default: the strongest the server offers.

security-mode.description: opcua-client: message security mode. Default: the strongest mode of the chosen policy.

pki-dir.description: opcua-client: directory holding the client certificate (cert.pem, key.pem), generated self-signed on first use. Needed for any policy but None; the server must trust it.

read-mode.description: opcua-client: how values arrive. poll (default): one batched Read per scan class per tick. subscribe: one OPC UA subscription per scan class (publishing interval = the class rate), the server sending values when they change. Quality, __Online and reconnect behave the same in both.

reassert-on-reconnect.description: opcua-client: when a lost session is re-established, command every output once more with the program's value, changed or not (default true). A server that restarted with its state reset holds its start-up values; without this an unchanged commanded value is never written again. Goes through the write gate: on a redundant pair only the leader sends it.

tags.description: runtime: binds input tags to the runtime's own health, so alarms and the historian can see it. Polled every scan-rate (default 1s); every status reads false / 0 until the first poll. A standby never scans, so these tags move only on the replica that leads. Beside field drivers under drivers:, or alone as driver:, where it keeps the memory loopback a project with no driver has. Any other driver type refuses tags:.

name.description: The input tag (declare it role: input).

task.description: main, or another task's name (an unnamed task's is its program's file name without the extension).

status.description: demoted (BOOL): the task's real-time priority was withdrawn, until restart. faulting (BOOL): its last scan raised a logic error. logic-errors, late, overruns (UDINT): counts since start.

anyOf.description: A connection template: an opcua-client section a devices: row names in driver:, with neither an endpoint (the row's) nor a manifest (derived from the profile).

endpoint.description: Listen address, opc.tcp://host:port (or host:port). Defaults to loopback: use opc.tcp://0.0.0.0:4840 to serve every interface.

application-uri.description: The server's ApplicationUri, the name an OPC UA client keys its connection on: an absolute URI. Defaults to urn:joyautomation:nautilus:<project>, the same on every host and replica; set it when two controllers run a project of the same name on one network.

pki.description: Certificate store directory, relative to the working directory: the server's own certificate and key (generated on first start) and the client certificates it trusts (trusted/certs) or has refused (rejected/certs). Approve a client with `naut opcua trust <thumbprint>`. Keep it out of git; `naut build` never embeds it.

writable.description: Globs over tag names or UDT member paths (TempSP, *_SP, Pump*.SpeedSP, Counts[2], Drives[*].Speed; [n] is an array index, [*] any index, no character classes) that a trusted OPC UA client may write: a session on a SignAndEncrypt channel whose certificate is in pki/trusted. A pattern on a tag opens its members. Inputs are never writable. The same globs and rule as sparkplug.writable, but its own list. Omit and the server is read-only.

anonymous-writes.description: Lab only: let an anonymous client on the None endpoint, with no certificate, write the tags writable opens, as a trusted client does (for simulators such as PLC-Lab or Factory I/O). Writable still decides what is writable. naut run logs a warning at start, an error when the endpoint listens beyond loopback. Never on a plant network.

sparkplug.description: Sparkplug B edge node. The MQTT password is NEVER here — set NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD.

broker.description: Broker URL, e.g. tcp://host:1883 or ssl://host:8883. Passed through to the MQTT client, which decides what it accepts, so no scheme is enforced here.

edge-node.description: Sparkplug edge node id. Defaults to the project name.

client-id.description: MQTT client id. Defaults to something derived from the edge node.

username.description: MQTT username. The password comes from NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD.

primary-host.description: Gate births on this SCADA host's STATE topic.

primary-host-offline.description: What the node does when the primary host's STATE goes offline. buffer (the default): stay connected and born, send no NDEATH, and stop publishing data until the host returns (store-forward buffers it and replays it as historical). disconnect: the Sparkplug 3.0 behaviour; publish NDEATH, disconnect, connect again with the next bdSeq, and birth once the host is back online. Needs primary-host.

publish-interval.description: How often changed metrics are published.

device.description: Removed. Each field connection is now its own Sparkplug device, named after its driver (eip, sparkplug-host) or its source id (modbus, snmp, redfish, prometheus), with its own DBIRTH/DDEATH. Delete this key; give a driver a name: to choose its device id.

writable.description: Globs over tag names or UDT member paths (Motor1.START, Pump*.SpeedSP) that NCMD/DCMD may write. A pattern on a tag opens its members. Omit and the node is read-only: every write is refused and only Node Control/Rebirth is honoured.

store-forward.description: Buffer up to this many data messages while the broker (or the primary host) is unreachable and replay them, marked historical, on reconnect. Omit to disable.

store-forward-file.description: Journal the store-forward buffer to this file so a restart, upgrade or crash during an outage does not lose it: the next start loads it and replays it, marked historical, after its first birth. Relative to the working directory. Omit to buffer in memory only (the default). Needs store-forward.

device-death-delay.description: Hold a device's DDEATH until its connection has been unhealthy this long (0 to 1m); one that recovers inside it sends no DDEATH and no DBIRTH. Default 0: DDEATH on the first unhealthy tick. Nothing is sent for the device while its death is held, so SCADA shows its last values with no quality and no updates. 1-5s suits a link known to blip.

flatten-udts.description: Publish each UDT member as a plain metric named by its path (P101/Running) instead of the tag as one Sparkplug Template, for hosts that do not read Templates. Commands address members by the same name.

default-class.description: Report-by-exception tuning applied to metrics with no class.

metric-classes.description: Glob patterns assigning metrics to a named class.

min-interval.description: Never publish this metric more often than this.

max-interval.description: Publish at least this often even when unchanged.

every-change.description: Publish every transition unconditionally (alarms, counters) — deadband and min-interval are ignored.

alarms.description: Turn BOOL tags into ISA-18.2 alarm state: an active list, acknowledge, shelve, and an append-only journal behind /api/alarms. Rules cover the UDT members (a handful of them cover a whole fleet, because a fleet is the same types repeated); `defs` are the standalone BOOLs that name themselves. Omit the section entirely and the controller runs exactly as it did before alarms existed.

shelve-times.description: The shelf durations an operator screen offers, served on /api/meta. Default 5m 15m 30m 1h 2h 4h 8h.

notify.description: Where events go besides the journal. Notifiers run off the scan goroutine on a bounded queue: a slow endpoint drops events with a counter rather than stalling the scan.

escalation.description: Escalation policies: page people about alarms nobody has acknowledged, level by level. The first policy (in order) whose match covers an alarm, and whose `when:` window covers the moment it began waiting, runs it. Only `naut run` pages; tests never do.

rules.description: Generate definitions in bulk by matching a struct TYPE and member, or a tag glob. File order, FIRST MATCH WINS, materialized once at load.

defs.description: Explicit definitions, one per condition — the standalone BOOLs a rule cannot generalize.

site-from.description: Regexp over the TAG NAME whose first capture group becomes a definition's site, e.g. "^([A-Z]+[0-9]+)_" turns RTU9_ZONE15_FIT_001 into site RTU9. Site is the alarm table's sort and filter axis and the `{site}` placeholder in a rule's templates. Omit it and site is empty.

area-from.description: The same, for area — the second axis, e.g. "^[A-Z]+[0-9]+_([A-Z]+[0-9]+)_".

alarm-defaults.description: What a definition gets when it does not say for itself. A value a rule or an entry spelled explicitly is never overwritten.

priority.description: Default priority. The package default is medium.

on-delay.description: How long the condition must hold before it annunciates — host-side qualification.

off-delay.description: How long it must stay clear before it returns to normal.

ack-required.description: false collapses unack-active to ack-active and unack-rtn to normal on arrival: annunciate-only, no operator workflow. Default true.

auto-clear.description: false means latched — clearing the field bit does not discharge the operator's obligation to see it. Default true.

shelve.description: Whether an operator may shelve it. Default true.

enable.description: A BOOL that must be true or the definition is Suppressed. Pointing it at a site's online flag is what stops a dead edge node from freezing four alarms on.

alarm-journal.description: The always-on in-memory ring, plus an optional durable sink. The ring sits in front of every sink, so the journal view works on a box with no database at all, and it is bounded by construction — the answer to a flapping storm.

sink.description: An additional durable journal. Omit it for the ring alone.

path.description: Where the `file` sink writes JSONL, inside the project. Rotated at a size cap.

dsn-env.description: The ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE holding the postgres sink's connection string — never the string itself, because a manifest is committed and a password in git is a password you have to rotate. Default NAUTILUS_ALARM_DB_URL, falling back to DATABASE_URL.

alarm-oncall.description: Who is on call. Rosters name people (a user name, or oidc:<name>), never addresses.

timezone.description: IANA time zone rosters and `when:` windows are read in, e.g. America/Chicago. Default UTC.

ack-url.description: The HMI as a person paged reaches it, e.g. https://hmi.plant.example:8443. Email and SMS pages then carry a link that acknowledges that alarm's occurrence: single use, at most 24 h. Empty: no link. Must be https unless ack-url-insecure: true.

ack-url-insecure.description: Allow an http:// ack-url. The link acknowledges as the person paged, so plaintext is an explicit choice: naut check warns, and naut run journals it at start.

ack-from-notification.description: What an ack link needs. link (default): the link alone acknowledges, as the person it was sent to, if they still hold ack. sign-in: only a browser signed in as that person may use it.

inbound.description: Take acknowledgements back through the SMS and voice provider: an SMS reply "ACK <code>", a keypress on the call. Off when absent. Not with ack-from-notification: sign-in.

url.description: This controller as the provider reaches it, exactly (https). The provider's signature is checked against it; SMS replies go to <url>/alarm-inbound/sms.

channels.description: The kinds that take replies: sms, voice, or both. Each must be a configured channel.

rosters.description: On-call rosters; a level names one as roster:<id>.

alarm-roster.description: One roster. Either `members` (everyone always, or one at a time with `rotate`), or `shifts`.

id.description: Named by a level as roster:<id>.

members.description: People: a user name (alice) or oidc:<name>. Without rotate, all are on call all the time.

rotate.description: One member at a time, in order, changing at each handover.

start.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the first member's first turn. A weekly rotation hands over on this date's weekday.

shifts.description: Shifts by time of day: whoever's shift covers the moment is on call.

alarm-shift.description: One shift: a window and who works it. A shift past midnight belongs to the day it starts on.

alarm-window.description: A time-of-day window. to not after from runs past midnight; from == to is 24 hours from from.

alarm-days.description: Days of the week: mon … sun, or a range like mon-fri. Empty is every day.

when.description: Only for alarms that began waiting inside this window (in alarms.oncall.timezone). The policy then runs to the end.

levels.description: In order of `after`. No fixed cap.

stop.description: ack (default): only an acknowledgement, a shelf or a suppression stops it. ack-or-rtn: a return to normal does too.

alarm-escalation-match.description: Which alarms a policy covers. Every field is optional; they AND together. Globs are case-insensitive.

alarm-channels.description: The ways a level's via: pages a person beyond the log (#715). Nothing secret here: credentials are in alarm-secrets.json and addresses in alarm-contacts.json, in the controller's state directory (naut alarms secrets|contacts).

alarm-channel-push.description: Web Push to the phones people subscribed through the HMI (#722). The VAPID key is the secret push.vapid-key in alarm-secrets.json (made at first start on a controller that is not half of a pair; naut alarms secrets generate push.vapid-key otherwise). A pair needs the same file on both boxes.

subject.description: A mailto: address or an https: URL the site owns. Push services (Google, Apple, Mozilla) may use it to reach you, and it is sent with every page, so it is never defaulted.

allow-hosts.description: The push services the controller may send to: host names (fcm.googleapis.com) or wildcards under one (*.push.apple.com). Empty: any public host. A private address is refused unless named here (a site's own push relay).

alarm-channel-email.description: Email over SMTP, always over TLS (STARTTLS or implicit) with the certificate verified.

smtp.description: The server, host:port (587 for STARTTLS, 465 implicit).

tls.description: How TLS starts. Default starttls: a server that does not offer it is refused.

username.description: Signs in with AUTH PLAIN, only once TLS is up. The password is the secret email.password.

ca-file.description: A PEM bundle on the box to verify the server's certificate against, instead of the system roots: how a site with its own CA keeps verification on.

insecure.description: Do not verify the server's certificate and, for a channel that sends no credential, allow plaintext. A password or token never crosses plaintext either way. naut check warns; naut run journals it at start.

alarm-channel-provider.description: SMS or voice through a Twilio-compatible REST API, over https. The token is the secret sms.token or voice.token.

provider.description: The API's base URL, https (e.g. https://api.twilio.com).

account.description: The account id the API path and basic auth name.

from.description: The number messages and calls come from, E.164 (+15550100).

ca-file.description: A PEM bundle on the box to verify the server's certificate against, instead of the system roots: how a site with its own CA keeps verification on.

insecure.description: Do not verify the server's certificate and, for a channel that sends no credential, allow plaintext. A password or token never crosses plaintext either way. naut check warns; naut run journals it at start.

alarm-channel-webhook.description: Each page POSTed as JSON (the person as a principal, never an address), for a paging service or a chat bridge.

url.description: An https URL (http only with insecure: true and no header).

header.description: The header carrying the secret webhook.header, e.g. Authorization.

ca-file.description: A PEM bundle on the box to verify the server's certificate against, instead of the system roots: how a site with its own CA keeps verification on.

insecure.description: Do not verify the server's certificate and, for a channel that sends no credential, allow plaintext. A password or token never crosses plaintext either way. naut check warns; naut run journals it at start.

alarm-level.description: One level: who, by which channels, how long after the alarm began waiting.

after.description: How long after the alarm began waiting this level is sent. Default 0s.

notify.description: roster:<id> (whoever is on call when it is sent) or a person (alice, oidc:carol).

via.description: Channel kinds; each person gets one send per kind. log is always there; email, sms, voice, webhook and push when alarms.channels configures them. email, sms and voice need the person's address in the contacts file on the box (naut alarms contacts set); push needs the person to have subscribed a phone in the HMI.

alarm-notify.description: One notifier: either `log: true` or `webhook: <url>`, never both in one entry.

log.description: Write every event to the structured log — often the only notifier a site needs, since a journal that also lands in the log stream is searchable by whatever already collects logs.

webhook.description: POST each event as JSON to this URL. Retries a couple of times, then drops rather than stalling the scan.

header.description: Header name for the webhook's API key (default Authorization).

header-env.description: Environment variable holding the webhook's API key. Same rule as the DSN: the secret is never in the file.

alarm-match.description: What a rule claims. All three are globs (*, ?, [class]); an empty field means any. A rule with no `member` matches only FLAT BOOL tags, and one with a `member` matches only struct members — a struct tag is not itself a BOOL, so "which member" is never a detail a rule can leave out.

type.description: The UDT name of a struct tag, as the project's ST declares it.

tag.description: A glob on the tag name.

alarm-rule.description: Generate definitions in bulk: name the (type, member) pair once and every matching tag gets an instance. First match wins across the rule list, and the expansion is materialized at load, never per scan — `naut alarms list` dumps the result so a few rules covering thousands of alarms stays auditable, not magic.

id.description: The definition's id. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Default "{path}".

name.description: The human-readable identity an operator reads. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Default "{desc} {member}".

site.description: Site. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Defaults to the tag's own, from `site-from`.

area.description: Area. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Defaults to the tag's own, from `area-from`.

display.description: Display path. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces.

on-delay.description: How long the condition must hold before it annunciates.

off-delay.description: How long it must stay clear before it returns to normal.

enable.description: A BOOL that must be true, else Suppressed. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. e.g. "{site}__Online".

suppress-when.description: A BOOL whose TRUE suppresses the alarm by design (a low-flow alarm while its pump is stopped). Only a readable TRUE suppresses: a path that cannot be read shows the alarm, with a warning, and naut check refuses it. Template, e.g. "{tag}.Stopped".

suppress-reason.description: The reason a suppress-when suppression shows on the alarm's row; default "<path> is true". Template.

equipment.description: The piece of plant the alarm belongs to: the unit an operator takes out of service (naut alarms out-of-service). Template; default "{tag}", the struct the rule matched.

consequence.description: What happens if nobody responds: the master alarm database's consequence column, read by naut alarms master. Copied to every alarm the rule generates; plain text, not a template.

response.description: What the operator does when it sounds (the corrective action). Copied to every alarm the rule generates; plain text, not a template.

alarm-rationalization.description: Where the alarm stands in ISA-18.2 rationalization. A reviewed or approved alarm names who reviewed it and the day.

state.description: pending (the default), reviewed by the team, or approved under management of change.

by.description: Who reviewed or approved it. Required unless pending.

at.description: The day, YYYY-MM-DD. Required unless pending.

alarm.description: One alarm definition: the BOOL condition to watch and the operator policy that governs it.

id.description: The identity everywhere — row key, ack target, journal id. Defaults to `tag`.

tag.description: The condition PATH: a flat tag ("PumpFault") or one member of a struct tag ("FIT_001.HH"). Must resolve to a BOOL; true means in alarm. A path that does not resolve is Suppressed with a reason, never an error — one dark site must not fault the engine.

name.description: The human-readable identity. Defaults to the id.

on-delay.description: How long the condition must hold before it annunciates.

off-delay.description: How long it must stay clear before it returns to normal.

enable.description: A BOOL that must be true, else Suppressed.

suppress-when.description: A BOOL whose TRUE suppresses the alarm by design. Only a readable TRUE suppresses: a path that cannot be read shows the alarm, with a warning, and naut check refuses it.

suppress-reason.description: The reason a suppress-when suppression shows; default "<path> is true".

equipment.description: The piece of plant the alarm belongs to, the unit an operator takes out of service. Default: the tag its condition is in.

consequence.description: What happens if nobody responds: the master alarm database's consequence column, read by naut alarms master.

response.description: What the operator does when it sounds (the corrective action).

siemens-target.description: A Siemens S7-1500 CPU as the deploy target: the writer emits SCL, tiad (the TIA Portal Openness agent) compiles and downloads, and the PLC Web API carries live values. The tiad token is never here: NAUTILUS_TIAD_TOKEN or NAUTILUS_TIAD_TOKEN_FILE.

group.description: Block group nautilus owns in the TIA project (default nautilus).

block-prefix.description: Prefix for every generated block, DB and tag table name (default naut_), so a generated block never collides with TIA's own (Main [OB1]) or a customer's. Empty is refused.

siemens-station.description: The CPU's whole hardware config. One CPU has exactly one station spec: a download replaces the whole config.

modules.description: Local modules next to the CPU. Slot 1 is the CPU's own.

siemens-cpu.description: The controller. In a repo, use a documentation address (192.0.2.x).

name.description: Device name in the TIA project, e.g. PLC_1.

address.description: IPv4 address of the PROFINET interface.

profinet-name.description: The CPU's PROFINET name of station: lowercase, explicit.

configuration-protection.description: FW 3.1 protection of the CPU's confidential configuration data. password (the default): protected, with the password from the secret store, never this file. none: off, an explicit choice. keep: leave the project's setting as found (an adopted station).

access-control.description: The CPU's PLC access control (users and roles). full-access-user (the default): access control on, with one user, nautilus, holding the runtime right Full access; its password comes from the secret store, never this file. keep: leave the project's access control and users as found (an adopted station).

siemens-web-server.description: Turns on the CPU's web server, which carries the Web API. Passwords are never here.

input-start.description: First %I byte; TIA assigns it when absent.

output-start.description: First %Q byte; TIA assigns it when absent.

update-time.description: Default update time for devices, at least 16ms. A nautilus device (profinet-manifest) takes only 16ms, 32ms, 64ms, 128ms, 256ms or 512ms (powers of two at a 1ms send clock), not below its min-cycle; with none set, the deploy rounds up to the first of those at or above min-cycle.

siemens-device.description: An IO device: explicit (gsdml, dap, name, address, modules) or a reference to a nautilus PROFINET device's manifest (profinet-manifest + address).

profinet-manifest.description: Path to a nautilus PROFINET device manifest; the deploy expands it.

gsdml.description: GSDML file name, installed through tiad.

dap.description: Device access point ID in the GSDML.

update-time.description: Update time, at least 16ms. For a profinet-manifest device: 16ms, 32ms, 64ms, 128ms, 256ms or 512ms, not below its min-cycle; when absent (here and on the IO system), the deploy rounds up to the first of those at or above min-cycle.

siemens-device-module.description: A GSDML module placed by its module ID.

siemens-online.description: The Web API connection for live values. The password is never here: NAUTILUS_SIEMENS_PASSWORD.

user.description: Web server user to log in as.

cert-sha256.description: SHA-256 of the CPU's certificate, to pin it (CPUs ship self-signed certificates).
